To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a formal representation of the problem solving process and a formal representation of social recommendation are essential to enable automated reasoning in the domain of qualitative problem solving.

1) a tutoring system that supports creative problem solving should be able to brainstorm with the student; 2) the tutoring system should be able to provide heuristic-based feedback to the student, based on the student’s problem solving behavior and the problem solving behavior of other users; 3) the tutoring system can use the social network of the user to provide social recommendation to the user.

(1) the design of tutoring systems that support qualitative problem solving requires the integration of two types of support, (2) the two types of support can be implemented by means of two technologies, and (3) the two technologies can be implemented by using the formal representations and automated reasoning procedures that are introduced in the paper.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of an integrated cognitive and social tutoring system for creative problem solving.
the design of a tutor that provides cognitive and social support to students in order to facilitate the generation of ideas and their evaluation in computer supported creative problem solving.

the design and development of a tutoring system for computer supported problem solving, which is based on the following two key ideas: (i) the use of a brainstorming agent for generating and evaluating solution alternatives, and (ii) the use of community-data-driven social recommendations in order to provide students with additional information on the quality of their solution alternatives.

it is possible to support students in creative problem solving by providing them with feedback that is both cognitively and socially oriented.
a tutoring system that supports brainstorming can be designed in such a way that it provides cognitive and social support to students in a seamless and transparent manner.
